title: Multi-CAM Post Processor Generation + Machine-Specific Safety Sequences
description: Generate post processors for all open-format CAM systems (Mastercam, NX, CATIA, SolidCAM, PowerMill, GibbsCAM, CAMWorks, BobCAD, SprutCAM). Build Phase B re-optimizer for closed systems (hyperMILL, Tebis, Edgecam). Create machine-specific safety sequences (startup/shutdown, tool change, coolant, spindle warm-up). Build multi-channel/mill-turn support for complex machines.

units.title: Mastercam .pst + NX TCL post processor templates
steps: Create PRISM Mastercam .pst post processor template:
Mastercam post format: text-based control definition file
Map Mastercam NCI codes to ToolpathBlock[] extraction
Extract: tool data, operation type, stock model, material from Mastercam context
Communication: HTTP call to PRISM server (Mastercam 2024+ supports HTTP from posts)
Fallback: standard post + sidecar JSON export
Create PRISM NX/Siemens TCL post processor:
NX post format: TCL/Tk scripting (mom_xxx procedures)
Map NX MOM variables to PRISM context (mom_tool_diameter, mom_spindle_speed, etc.)
Extract: UDE (User Defined Events), tool data, operation data from NX context
Communication: TCL HTTP call to PRISM server
Fallback: standard post + sidecar JSON
Both posts follow same pipeline architecture as Fusion .cps: extract context → call PRISM → write output
exit_conditions: Mastercam .pst loads and runs in Mastercam 2024+
NX TCL post loads in NX 2306+
Both posts extract tool and operation context
Both communicate with PRISM server when available
Both fall back gracefully when server is down

units.title: CATIA/SolidCAM/PowerMill/GibbsCAM/CAMWorks/BobCAD/SprutCAM post templates
steps: Create post processor templates for remaining open-format CAM systems:
CATIA Manufacturing: PP word table + VB macro — extract APT source, call PRISM
SolidCAM: .gpp config file — define variables, map to PRISM context
PowerMill: .opt option file + macro — OMF format extraction, PRISM call
GibbsCAM: .pit post template — CL data extraction, PRISM call
CAMWorks: TechDB + post config — technology database integration
BobCAD: post processor config file — block format definition, PRISM bridge
SprutCAM: CLData script post — script-based extraction, PRISM call
Each template follows the same pattern:
1. Extract context from CAM-specific API
2. Build PRISM job JSON (machine, tools, operations, stock, material)
3. HTTP POST to PRISM server
4. Receive optimized G-code, write output
5. Fallback: standard output + sidecar JSON
Tribal knowledge integration: include CAM-specific tips from 2,800+ tip database
exit_conditions: Post templates created for all 7 CAM systems
Each template extracts minimum viable context (tool + operation + material)
HTTP communication pattern consistent across all CAM systems
Sidecar JSON format identical regardless of source CAM

units.title: Phase B Re-Optimizer for closed systems (hyperMILL, Tebis, Edgecam, any G-code source)
steps: Build standalone Phase B re-optimization pipeline:
Input: G-code file (from any source — hyperMILL, Tebis, manual programming, legacy)
G-code parser extracts: moves, tool changes, spindle/feed commands, canned cycles
User provides context via MCP/chat or config file: machine, material, tools, tolerances
Run pipeline stages 1-5 (skip Stage 0 normalization — already have G-code)
Stage 6 re-generates optimized G-code preserving original structure but with optimized S/F
Preserve: program structure, comments, sub-program calls, custom M-codes
Replace: S/F values, add controller optimization codes, insert safety checks
PRISM CLI command: `prism optimize input.nc --machine DMU50 --material 316L --output optimized.nc`
MCP action: pp_reoptimize — accepts G-code string + context, returns optimized G-code
Skill: /post-optimize for interactive re-optimization via chat
exit_conditions: hyperMILL G-code successfully re-optimized with variable S/F
Original program structure preserved (comments, sub-programs, custom M-codes)
Re-optimized output passes PostProcessorVerificationEngine validation
CLI and MCP action both functional
15+ tests comparing before/after optimization metrics

units.title: Machine-specific safety sequences — startup, shutdown, tool change, spindle warm-up
steps: Build MachineSequenceEngine: machine-specific operational sequences
Startup sequences per machine type:
Vertical mill: G28 G91 Z0 / G90 G17 G21 G40 G80 / T1 M6 / etc.
Horizontal mill: includes pallet/tombstone orientation check
5-axis: includes rotary axis home + TCPC activation
Lathe: chuck close verify, tailstock check, turret home
Mill-turn: mode switch (milling↔turning), spindle select (main/sub/live)
Tool change sequences per ATC type:
Side-mount ATC: Z home → orient spindle → tool change → new tool measure
Umbrella ATC: Z home → rapid to change position → change → rapid back
Turret: direct index → no Z home needed
Magazine: random vs fixed pocket logic
Coolant management:
Flood: M8 on → cutting → M9 off → chip blow M7 (optional)
TSC: M88 (through-spindle on) at specified pressure
MQL: M7 with flow rate setting
Cryogenic: specialized M-codes per system (LN2/CO2)
Spindle warm-up: configurable warm-up cycle (5 min ramp for cold starts)
Shutdown: retract, coolant off, spindle stop, home position, program end
exit_conditions: Startup sequence differs between vertical mill and 5-axis
Tool change sequence appropriate for machine ATC type
Coolant codes match machine capability
Warm-up cycle optional and configurable

units.title: Multi-channel / Mill-turn support
steps: Build MultiChannelPostEngine for complex machine types:
Mill-turn:
Channel 1 (main spindle): turning operations
Channel 2 (sub-spindle): simultaneous turning or part transfer
Channel 3 (live tooling): milling operations with C-axis
Synchronization codes: WAITM (Siemens), !-codes (Mazak), M-code sync (Fanuc)
Mode switching: G12.1 (polar interpolation), C-axis lock/unlock, CSS mode (G96/G97)
Y-axis milling on lathes: offset handling, tool orientation
Sub-spindle transfer:
Part handoff sequence: approach → grip → cut-off → retract
G14/G15 axis mirroring (Mazak), TRANSMIT (Siemens)
Bar feeder interface: bar advance, remnant detection
Swiss-type lathe:
Guide bushing ON/OFF modes
Sliding headstock coordination
Gang tooling vs turret selection
B-axis milling (where equipped)
Stream synchronization output per controller dialect
Multi-channel cycle time: parallel operation tracking
exit_conditions: Mill-turn program with main + sub-spindle + live tooling generates correctly
Synchronization codes inserted per controller dialect
Sub-spindle transfer sequence complete and safe
Multi-channel operations tracked for parallel cycle time
20+ tests covering mill-turn and multi-channel scenarios
